correctness.rationale: For each real four-data input, expand increments into three nodal steps; triangle inequality bounds output continuous variation by the largest step image variation, and single steps attain equality. Exact Lagrange cardinal identities give two reflected terminal steps and one central step. Their quadratic derivatives have both roots strictly inside (-1,1); signed-piece integration gives A and B. A increases, B decreases by the displayed negative logarithmic derivative, so their unique crossing minimizes the maximum. verify.py rederives identities, certifies crossing signs and value using rational integer-square-root enclosures, and separately samples 4000 random signals. No empirical enumeration is used as an infinite proof.

evidence: The bounded-variation seminorm is defined as the integral of |p'|, whereas the classical Lebesgue constant is the uniform function-value operator norm (Gunzburger–Teckentrup, arXiv:1407.3291v1, sections 1–2; Berrut–Trefethen 2004, sections 2–3).

The previously published symmetric-grid result studies extremal pointwise range escape for nondecreasing observations (full RESULT.md of 2026/10/26/SCOPE-optimal-symmetric-four-node-cubic-interpolation-for-monotone-ran--7f9a4d5c7ee7).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A nodal step decomposition is common to several interpolation problems, but equality of step values or peak excursion is not equality of their integrated derivative variation. There is no normalization, duality, or change of variables converting the pointwise Lebesgue or monotone range objective into the present discrete-to-continuous variation norm. The full previous proof provides the same step polynomials, creating adjacency and priority risk, but neither its bound nor its minimizer determines the newly calculated positive outer lobe or variation optimum.

value.rationale: The natural operator norm compares the total oscillation created on an entire interpolated interval against the total variation available in four samples. The theorem completely and sharply optimizes this stability invariant over the canonical symmetric four-node design family, balancing two distinct jump mechanisms. It reduces the gain from about 2.00685 at equally spaced nodes to 1.42359, a material stability difference, and shows a variation-optimal grid differing from the previously determined range-optimal grid. The result is a complete motivated design classification, not a general-name substitution or unexplained isolated numerical example.
